newsitem.title: FRANCE: Bosnia presidents meet in Paris to bolster peace.
newsitem.headline: Bosnia presidents meet in Paris to bolster peace.

text.p: Bosnia's three co-presidents met major world powers in Paris on Thursday to approve a two-year peace plan to strengthen peace in the former Yugoslav republic.

The Moslem, Serb and Croat presidents gathered in a Paris conference centre for one-day talks to pledge actions to complete joint institutions, enable the return of refugees, ensure freedom of movement and press freedom and build a market economy.

The international community will in return commit itself to continue assistance in rebuilding Bosnia's administration and economy after almost four years of war. International mediator Carl Bildt was co-chairing the conference with French Foreign Minister Herve de Charette.
"We had some good progress but a lot of work remains to be done to reunite the country," British Foreign Secretary Malcolm Rifkind said on arrival at the Kleber centre near the Arc de Triomphe.

Countries attending the three-hour conference are Bosnia, Croatia, rump Yugoslavia, the United States, Russia, France, Britain, Germany, Italy, Canada, the Netherlands, Ireland as president of the European Union, Turkey representing the Islamic Conference Organisation and several international organisations.

Next month, NATO is likely to approve a slimmed-down peacekeeping force to succeed the peace implementation force (IFOR) whose mandate expires at the end of 1996. Officials said the post-IFOR force was not on the agenda in Paris.
